theory: Hardy is an evidence-producing theorem-proving harness in which models propose, Lean checks, and the harness preserves what each artifact actually establishes. Its local layered design separates mathematical content, experimental measurements, runtime control, and human-readable claims.
instead_of: A proof chatbot could optimize for fluent completion and trust its own transcript; Hardy instead keeps explicit authority and identity boundaries even when that preserves partial or refused work.

absorption.rationale: New local capabilities and checks fit the design; distributed execution and independent confinement require new ownership boundaries.

world_mapping.rationale: Mathematical statements, formal evidence, documentary claims and experimental conditions map to separate domain concepts.

abstraction.rationale: Package contracts and owners reduce coupling, but interactive coordination and mode-specific execution still need substantial shared context.

justification.rationale: Verification and pooling explain their rejected shortcuts rather than relying on convention.

honest_limits.rationale: Partial, modulo, unreported and unverified states prevent mechanism from being presented as measured success.

rehearsals.requirement: Add another bounded retrieval source to proof search
rehearsals.why: The formal retrieval boundary already carries per-source provenance and budgets.

rehearsals.requirement: Run untrusted generated artifacts under a genuinely independent sandbox
rehearsals.why: Current child-process control and fresh reconstruction do not create confinement or an independent trusted image.

rehearsals.requirement: Coordinate multiple remote workers editing one durable project
rehearsals.why: Interactive records and capability lifetimes are designed around local ownership.
